newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Steep Belgian curve keeps OLO investors in armlock.
newsitem.headline: Steep Belgian curve keeps OLO investors in armlock.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were virtually unchanged in paper-thin trade ahead of the release of U.S. jobs data on Thursday, with dealers expecting little movement of the OLO/Bund spread and the yield curve.

OLO futures were up three basis points at 121.55 with only 67 lots traded (compared to more than 50,000 Bund future contracts in London). The 2007 benchmark OLO yield was down one bp at 5.71 bp, eight bp over Bunds.
Dealers said that the steep yield curve -- three-month T-bills yield 3.23/28 percent -- would force investors to stay in bonds in the weeks and months ahead.
